title: Bounded below injective descent and shift-compatible comparison
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal A'$ be abelian categories with enough injectives [def-sp-abelian; def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Write $K^+(\mathcal A)$ for the homotopy category of bounded below integer cochain complexes, $D^+(\mathcal A)$ for its localization at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category; def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories], and $K^+(\operatorname{Inj}\mathcal A)$ for the full subcategory on complexes with injective terms. Let $\mathcal B$ be an abelian category and let $F:K^+(\mathcal A)\to K^+(\mathcal B)$ and $F':K^+(\mathcal A')\to K^+(\mathcal B)$ be exact functors, equipped with their shift comparisons [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Let $E:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A'$ be additive and exact, and also write $E$ for its termwise functor and $D^+E$ for the induced derived functor. Suppose $\tau:F\Rightarrow F'E$ is a natural transformation on homotopy categories compatible with the shift comparisons.
There are exact functors $RF:D^+(\mathcal A)\to D^+(\mathcal B)$ and $RF':D^+(\mathcal A')\to D^+(\mathcal B)$ computed by applying $F,F'$ to bounded below injective representatives. For $K$, choose quasi-isomorphisms $k:K\to I$ and $k':EK\to J$ to bounded below complexes of injectives. Choose a chain map $u:EI\to J$ such that $u\circ E(k)$ and $k'$ are homotopic. The morphism represented by
$$F(I)\xrightarrow{\tau_I}F'(EI)\xrightarrow{F'(u)}F'(J)$$
defines a natural transformation $R\tau:RF\Rightarrow RF'\circ D^+E$, independent of $I,J,k,k',u$ under the canonical comparison isomorphisms. It is natural for every morphism in $D^+(\mathcal A)$, including morphisms $K\to L[1]$, and commutes with the induced shift comparisons. The construction respects identity and composition of such comparison data. No assumption that $EI$ has injective terms is required.

source.place: Tag 05TK, lemma-resolution-functor-quasi-inverse (bounded below injective equivalence); agent-stated descent of a shift-compatible transformation across an exact functor, using K-injective comparison. Compare the adjacent resolution-functor discussion; no unbounded assertion.

proof.text:
Use [lem-trf-filtered-localization-injective-model] on the fixed filtration interval $[0,0]$. In the notation of [def-sp-filtration], an object then has $F^pM=M$ for $p\leq0$ and $F^pM=0$ for $p\geq1$. Its only nonzero graded object is $\operatorname{gr}^0M=M$. Thus filtered maps and filtered homotopies are exactly ordinary maps and homotopies; filtered quasi-isomorphisms are exactly quasi-isomorphisms; filtered injectives are exactly injectives. The fixed-interval exact equivalence asserted by the cited node is therefore
$$q_{\mathcal A}:K^+(\operatorname{Inj}\mathcal A)\xrightarrow{\sim}D^+(\mathcal A).$$
It also supplies the same equivalence for $\mathcal A'$. This is a specialization of an existing stronger statement, not a new assertion about filtered categories.

source.place: Tag 05TK, lemma-resolution-functor-quasi-inverse; equivalently Tag 015Q in the one-step filtration interval

proof.text:
Write $q_{\mathcal A}$ as part of an adjoint equivalence $q_{\mathcal A}\dashv h_{\mathcal A}$ and give the quasi-inverse $h_{\mathcal A}$ the shift isomorphisms conjugate to those of $q_{\mathcal A}$ through the unit and counit; by this construction the unit and counit commute with the shifts. Since $q_{\mathcal A}$ is exact, [lem-sf-triangulated-right-adjoint] shows that $h_{\mathcal A}$ is exact; likewise for $h_{\mathcal A'}$. Write $i_{\mathcal A}$ for the full inclusion of injective complexes into $K^+(\mathcal A)$ and $Q_{\mathcal B}:K^+(\mathcal B)\to D^+(\mathcal B)$ for localization. Set
$$RF=Q_{\mathcal B}F i_{\mathcal A}h_{\mathcal A},\qquad RF'=Q_{\mathcal B}F'i_{\mathcal A'}h_{\mathcal A'}.$$
The inclusions are exact: shifts retain injective terms, and the terms of a cone are finite sums of injectives, which are injective since a map into each summand extends separately across a monomorphism. Localization carries cone triangles to distinguished triangles [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Consequently these composites are exact, using the assumed exactness of $F,F'$ and the definition of an exact functor [def-weil-triangulated-category]. On an injective representative $I$, the equivalence identifies $RF(Q_{\mathcal A}I)$ with $Q_{\mathcal B}F(I)$, naturally for every homotopy class between injective representatives.

source.place: Tags 05TK and 05TJ, lemma-resolution-functor-quasi-inverse and lemma-resolution-functor; paragraph lemma-j-is-exact

proof.text: For a bounded below representative $K$, choose $k:K\to I$ and $k':EK\to J$ using [lem-sc-bounded-below-injective-resolution-existence] in $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal A'$. Exactness of $E$ gives its termwise derived functor and canonical shift comparison by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. These restrict to bounded below categories: a termwise image of a complex zero in degrees below $a$ is again zero there. It sends $k$ to a quasi-isomorphism: exactness identifies $E(\ker d)/E(\operatorname{im}d)$ with $E(\ker d/\operatorname{im}d)$, so $H^n(Ek)=E(H^n(k))$. Both $I,J$ are K-injective by [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective]. From now on use the canonical localization comparisons to write $D^+E(QK)=Q(EK)$. No injectivity assertion about $EI$ occurs.

Because $J$ is K-injective, [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] lifts the derived morphism
$$Q(k')\,Q(Ek)^{-1}:Q(EI)\longrightarrow QJ$$
to a unique homotopy class $u:EI\to J$. Here $D^+$ is the localization of $K^+$ as in the statement: for bounded below sources and bounded below injective targets, the bijection between homotopy classes and morphisms of this localization is the Hom clause of [lem-trf-filtered-localization-injective-model] on the interval $[0,0]$ (Step 1), and it agrees with the bounded below clause of [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]; the same applies to every use of the Hom bijection below. The images of $u\circ E(k)$ and $k'$ agree after localization; the same Hom bijection with source $EK$ and target $J$ shows they agree in the homotopy category. Thus any chain representative $u$ has the homotopy required in the statement, and all such representatives give the same $F'(u)$. Define the component $t_K=Q_{\mathcal B}(F'(u)\tau_I)$, using Step 2 to identify its source with $RF(K)$ and its target with $RF'(D^+E(K))$.

source.place: Tag 05TG, lemma-morphisms-into-injective-complex; Tag 070I, lemma-K-injective, Hom bijection

proof.text:
Let $\alpha:QK\to QL$ be any derived morphism. Choose resolutions $k_K:K\to I_K$, $k_L:L\to I_L$ and $k'_K:EK\to J_K$, $k'_L:EL\to J_L$ as above. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], let $a:I_K\to I_L$ and $b:J_K\to J_L$ represent
$$Qa=Qk_L\,\alpha\,(Qk_K)^{-1},\qquad Qb=Qk'_L\,(D^+E)(\alpha)\,(Qk'_K)^{-1}.$$
Substituting $Qu_X=Qk'_X\,Q(Ek_X)^{-1}$ and the exact-$E$ localization comparison gives $Q(bu_K)=Q(u_LEa)$. The Hom bijection with source $EI_K$ and K-injective target $J_L$ gives $bu_K=u_LEa$ in the homotopy category. Naturality of $\tau$ at $a$ now gives
$$F'(b)F'(u_K)\tau_{I_K}=F'(u_L)F'(Ea)\tau_{I_K}=F'(u_L)\tau_{I_L}F(a).$$
After $Q_{\mathcal B}$ this is precisely naturality of $t$. The argument allowed every $\alpha$, so it includes every $K\to L[1]$, without restricting to chain maps between $K,L$.

source.place: Tags 05TG and 070I; comparison-square argument in lemma-resolution-functor

proof.text: For two choices of source resolution over $K$, the Hom bijection [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] gives the unique comparison $a:I\to\widetilde I$ with $Qa=Q\widetilde k\,(Qk)^{-1}$; similarly it gives $b:J\to\widetilde J$. Both are homotopy equivalences: lift the inverse derived arrows by the same bijection, and its injectivity makes both composites identities. Their defining augmentation equations also hold up to homotopy by that bijection. Thus $F(a),F'(b)$ are isomorphisms in the homotopy category. The calculation of Step 5 with $\alpha=1_{QK}$ says $F'(b)t_K=\widetilde t_KF(a)$, with localization understood. These are exactly the canonical comparison isomorphisms from Step 2. Their uniqueness makes comparisons for three choices compose, so the component is independent of $I,J,k,k'$; uniqueness of $u$ in Step 4 handles its choice too. Choosing the representatives supplied by $h_{\mathcal A},h_{\mathcal A'}$ gives a natural transformation of the two fixed functors, and the preceding equality identifies every other computation with it.

source.place: Tags 05TJ and 05TK, uniqueness of resolution comparisons; remark-big-localization immediately after 05TK

proof.text:
Compute the component at $K[1]$ with $I[1],J[1],k[1],k'[1]$, identifying $E(K[1])$ with $(EK)[1]$ by the termwise shift isomorphism. The comparison is $u[1]$: shifting the homotopy $uE(k)\simeq k'$ gives its defining equation. Denote the given shift isomorphisms for $F,F'$ by $s_F,s_{F'}$. The hypothesis on $\tau$ is
$$s_{F',EI}\,\tau_{I[1]}=\tau_I[1]\,s_{F,I},$$
with the termwise $E$ comparison inserted. Naturality of $s_{F'}$ at $u$ gives
$$s_{F',J}\,F'(u[1])\tau_{I[1]}=(F'(u)\tau_I)[1]\,s_{F,I}.$$
These are the induced shift comparisons of Step 2 when computed with shifted resolutions, so this is the required shift square for $R\tau$. Step 6 transfers it to any chosen resolutions of $K[1]$. The same calculation works for every integer shift and hence retains the coherence of the given shift structures.

source.place: lemma-j-is-exact, displayed comparison for j(K[1]); agent calculation of the transformation shift square

proof.text:
For identity comparison data take $E=1$, $F'=F$, $\tau=1$ and $I=J$, $k=k'$, $u=1_I$; the component is the identity. Step 6 gives the identity for arbitrary choices. For composable data $(E,\tau:F\to F'E)$ and $(E',\sigma:F'\to F''E')$, choose $I,J,H$ resolving $K,EK,E'EK$, with comparisons $u:EI\to J$ and $v:E'J\to H$ satisfying $uE(k)\simeq k'$ and $vE'(k')\simeq k''$. Then $w=vE'(u)$ satisfies $w(E'E)(k)\simeq k''$, since an additive termwise functor sends a homotopy $dh+hd$ to the same homotopy formula. It is therefore the comparison for the composite exact functor. Naturality of $\sigma$ at $u$ gives
$$F''(v)\sigma_JF'(u)\tau_I=F''(v)F''(E'u)\sigma_{EI}\tau_I=F''(w)(\sigma_{EI}\tau_I).$$
The left side computes the composite of the two derived comparisons and the right side computes the comparison of the composite data. Step 6 proves this for arbitrary choices. For three comparisons, both ways give the same iterated composite by associativity. Thus identity and composition are respected, with no requirement that $EI$ or $E'J$ be injective.

split_report.summary: Split into eight steps using existing nodes only. Specialized the existing filtered equivalence to filtration interval [0,0], then constructed the comparison via the K-injective Hom bijection and proved arbitrary-derived-morphism naturality, all choice independence, shift compatibility, and identity/composition by explicit equations. No change to the statement and no assumption that E preserves injectives.
split_report.blueprint: Serves lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map proof clauses "One may compute the cone on an injective resolution" and "All the cone maps and Kummer boundaries commute with pullback of the pair and its trivialized line bundle", through step 10 of lem-amb-relative-torsor-cohomology: resolve the relative fibre functor and descend its natural comparison, including boundary shifts.

tool_uses.why: Its fixed interval [0,0] specialization supplies the exact bounded-injective equivalence; this is a generic resolution tool, not a replacement of the Cartier/Kummer unit route.
Generic Hom bijection into a K-injective target proves the unique comparison and equality of homotopy classes; no scheme-specific route is imported.
